evals.name: happy-path-sync
evals.prompt: Can you run the upstream sync and see if anything new came in? If there's a PR, tell me what's in it and whether it's ready to merge.
evals.expected_output: Triggers the Upstream Sync workflow, watches it to completion, checks for an auto-opened PR, reports PR number/URL/diff-stat if one exists, or 'no new upstream' if not. Correctly uses `--repo zjean/server` flag, does NOT push to upstream-main directly, does NOT target Sync-in/server for the PR.

evals.name: conflict-resolution
evals.prompt: The upstream-sync workflow just opened PR #99 on zjean/server and it's CONFLICTING. Get it merged.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes that upstream-main is workflow-writable only, closes PR #99 with a superseded comment, branches off main, merges origin/upstream-main into it with --no-ff, resolves conflicts (correctly prefers upstream for overlapping i18n keys, preserves our custom keys), runs builds to verify, commits via `rtk proxy git commit --no-edit` (not plain `git commit --no-edit`), does NOT use `git add -A` (would sweep in unrelated `.claude/` working-tree state), pushes the new branch, opens a replacement PR targeting zjean/server with merge-commit strategy noted in the body. After the user reports the PR is merged, also fast-forwards local main and deletes the local sync branch.

evals.name: investigate-custom-ui-impact
evals.prompt: An upstream sync just merged into main. It touched some backend/src/applications/files/ code. Do we need to update anything in our custom v2/v3 UI, and if so what exactly?
evals.expected_output: Identifies the upstream commits via `git log origin/main..origin/upstream-main` or equivalent, diffs each interesting commit, classifies changes as wire-contract / internal-refactor / behaviour-change, greps custom-v2/ and shared classic services for callers, produces a scannable report with concrete before/after patches where wire contracts changed, and a 'No impact' section or explicit recommendations. Does NOT silently apply edits — the investigation is the deliverable.

evals.name: port-classic-styles-to-v2-tokens
evals.prompt: Upstream just shipped a new markdown viewer in `frontend/src/app/applications/files/components/viewers/files-viewer-markdown.component.{ts,html,scss}`. I want the same viewer in our v2 custom UI. Port it.
evals.expected_output: Builds a v2 viewer under `custom-v2/preview/` and wires it into FileDetailComponent (signal-based load/lock/save lifecycle), but BEFORE shipping does a token-translation pass on the styles: identifies every `var(--si-*)` reference the classic source uses, flags ones that don't exist in v2 (`--si-bg`, `--si-danger`, classic-flavored fallbacks like `#fff`/`#111`/`#c0392b`), and replaces them with the right v2 token (`--si-bg0` for canvas, `--si-bg1`/`--si-bg2` for raised surfaces, `--si-rose` for danger, drop fallbacks entirely). Removes any dead light/dark class plumbing. Browser-verifies the result against v2's always-dark navy palette (or at minimum, inspects computed styles at the host element). Catches the white-on-white bug that PR #202 fixed before it ships.
